question: Without canonical semantic slot names/IDs, can an engine discover a reusable typed semantic partition from raw language plus identically visible behavioral demonstrations, then ground unseen raw language into that discovered partition?

training_examples.behavior_signature: typed observable transition/extension behavior; no canonical predicate/slot identity

discovered_slots.slot_id: arbitrary engine-local identifier; surface name ignored by scorer

arguments: visible entity IDs in semantic argument order

denotational_equivalence.slot_alignment: maximum one-to-one matching using training denotation agreement first, then independent heldout denotation agreement; hidden canonical names never used
denotational_equivalence.valid_slot: all training members assigned to a slot must share one independently recomputed observable behavior signature and compatible argument types
denotational_equivalence.heldout_correctness: assignment is correct only if the aligned discovered slot has the same hidden denotation on independent probes and arguments/polarity/modality are correct
denotational_equivalence.partition_metric: pairwise same-slot/different-slot agreement over training examples after excluding ambiguous examples
denotational_equivalence.assignment_metric: heldout denotational assignment accuracy after label-free alignment
denotational_equivalence.exact_metric: all heldout assignments/abstentions and discovered partition correct up to slot permutation
